title: Balarila: Deep Learning for Semantic Grammar Error Correction in Low-Resource Settings
venue: Proceedings of the First Workshop in South East Asian Language Processing (co-located with EMNLP 2023)
tldr: Balarila demonstrates a practical, cost-effective transformer-based Filipino grammar checker using synthetic data, though its performance reveals ongoing challenges in low-resource NLP for complex semantic tasks.
problem_and_motivation: Existing Filipino grammar checkers like Gramatika are limited to lexical errors and rely on rule-based/statistical methods. No publicly available Filipino grammar checker can address semantic errors, which are more complex. Training data is scarce for low-resource Filipino language.
approach: Balarila adopts GECToR's iterative sequence tagging approach using transformer encoders (BERT Tagalog Base, RoBERTa Tagalog Base, RoBERTa Tagalog Large). An automated error generation pipeline creates synthetic datasets from scraped Filipino news articles (510,411 raw sentences). Two-stage fine-tuning: first on error-filled sentences, then on mixed error-free/error-filled sentences. 39 unique transformation tags covering grammatical and spelling errors.
findings: RoBERTa-Large achieved best F0.5 score of 70.75, with RoBERTa-Base at 69.00. RoBERTa-Base was most cost-effective (1.75% F0.5 difference with fewer resources). Models struggled with duplicate words, morphological errors, wrong punctuation marks, and missing words. Error-free sentences showed higher accuracy than error-filled sentences. The datasets serve as benchmark for Filipino GEC.

definitions.GEC: Grammar Error Correction - task of detecting and correcting grammatical errors in text
definitions.GED: Grammar Error Detection - task of identifying whether a sentence contains errors
definitions.GECToR: Grammatical Error Correction: Tag, Not Rewrite - sequence tagging approach for GEC
definitions.Transformation Tags: Tag-encoded edit operations applied to tokens to correct errors
definitions.Tagalog Enclitics: Small words (daw/din/roon/doon) that change based on preceding word's ending
definitions.Filipino Verb Forms: Forms created using aspect (completed, incompleted, contemplated, recently completed) and focus (actor-focus, object-focus)

citations.context: Filipino grammar checker using rule-based methods and SMT

high.justification: Directly applies NLP methods (transformer encoders, sequence tagging) to Filipino language processing for grammar error correction

medium.justification: Addresses low-resource language challenges in NLP, though not focused on psycholinguistics per se

limitations: Limited error coverage - only specific grammatical and spelling errors covered
Synthetic data may introduce bias and inaccuracy in error representations
RoBERTa-Large had memory issues during training due to GPU VRAM limitations
Error automation assumed one error per sentence, which is unrealistic
Inconsistency in correcting the same erroneous sentence with different error contexts
remember_this: Balarila demonstrates that transformer-based models can achieve reasonable Filipino grammar error correction (F0.5=70.75) using synthetic data, but challenges remain in handling complex semantic errors and low-resource NLP limitations.
